subject: Post-call: Integration hardening + JSON validation & retry pattern proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Scott <hannah@finlytic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Integration hardening + JSON validation & retry pattern proposal

Hi Hannah — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed plan so we can align next steps: 

1) Goals from your side (as I heard them):
   - Reliable structured outputs for scoring pipelines (JSON for customer data enrichment)
   - Deterministic reranker decisions (embeddings + short-context reranks)
   - Low error surface around schema drift and transient generator failures

2) Proposed integration/architecture approach (high level):
   - SDK onboarding: we'll provide a sample Node + Python snippet to wire auth and streaming.
   - Auth: short-lived service account tokens (mTLS optional) + role-restricted keys for inference/embeddings.
   - Routing: latency-first for critical requests, cost-fallback to smaller quantized variants when load spikes.
   - Structured output: constrained decoding + an explicit JSON schema that we validate server-side. On failure we retry with progressively constrained decoding and a short jittered backoff.
   - Embeddings / reranker: batch embeddings with async queueing; reranker uses a trimmed context and confidence gating (score threshold) before committing predictions to downstream store.

3) Immediate asks from Redwood to FinLytics:
   - Confirm requirement for hard schema validation vs permissive schema (we recommend strict for production).
   - Share a representative payload and two failing examples if available.
   - Procurement: contact for procurement (cc'd) to start the contract path for Dedicated capacity if you want predictable throughput.

Attachments: sample_structured_schema_v1.json (attached) — this is a starter schema and includes a validation+retry flow diagram in comments.

Next steps I propose: Marissa will produce a tailored sample integration (SDK + sample tests) within 48 hours; Rishi will outline the embedding/reranker configuration and validation metrics we should track. I'll coordinate a short technical review call after those deliverables (30 min).

If that all sounds good, reply with the preferred time window for our follow-up and provide the procurement contact.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration hardening + JSON validation & retry pattern proposal

Hannah — attaching a concrete artifact and notes. See sample_structured_schema_v1.json attached (lightweight): it includes
- required fields + enum constraints for known categories
- a "_schema_version" field so we can detect client/server drift
- a minimal post-generation validator spec (error codes and suggested corrective actions)

Example failure & retry flow (text):
- Gen attempt 1: model returns malformed JSON (missing required field). Server validator rejects with ERROR_SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD.
- Retry 1: server re-invokes generation with tighter decoding constraints (e.g., increased temperature->0, top_p->0.4, token_bias to forbid raw text tokens) and a stricter stop sequence.
- Retry 2 (if still invalid): call a smaller deterministic variant with prefix forcing (explicit JSON skeleton) and escalate a warning to the application.

On your SLA question: for Dedicated customers we provide latency SLOs per model class; for hosted we provide target p50/p95 and recommend canary routing for initial rollout. I'll include a short table in the shared Drive doc for your procurement review.

Attachments: sample_structured_schema_v1.json

I'll draft a short test harness (nyc-run unit + a few integration tests) that demonstrates the validator and the retry transitions — target delivery EOD Wednesday PT.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Scott <hannah@finlytic.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration hardening + JSON validation & retry pattern proposal

Looping in the engineering specifics so FinLytics knows what we'll ship: 

- Embeddings: recommend batched upsert every 5–10s with dedup and TTL lane for ephemeral items. We'll provide a sample pipeline that uses semantic hashing + cosine-thresholding to gate reranker inputs.
- Reranker: keep the candidate set <50, use short-context attention window to reduce cost, and compute a confidence score. Low-confidence outputs get routed to deterministic fallback.
- Validation metrics: percentage invalid JSON, retry rate, post-retry success rate, average retries per request, and end-to-end latency (p95). We'll ship a Grafana dashboard template.
- Retry pattern specifics: exponential backoff with jitter, deterministic model fallback on third attempt, and a configurable max-retries=3 by default. We'll include a "dry-run" mode in the SDK so you can test the validator without committing outputs to your DB.

I'll attach a short checklist in the Drive (link above) and push the reranker config as a gist for review.

—
